Synthetic gesture frames and hold durations intentionally model elapsed pointer time rather than app readiness.

The mocked recorder exposes no completion event after the minimum voice capture duration, so the stop button's readiness cannot be awaited. Reviewed 2026-09-04: still true. The seam this needs is a resolved state on the mock recorder that the stop control reflects, at which point the sleep becomes an ordinary toBeEnabled().
Opt-in performance benchmark requires CHAT_PERF_BENCH=1 and is intentionally excluded from the deterministic CI gate.

Asserts that pushing a cognia:// URL produces no console errors, and "nothing happened" has no event to await. Reviewed 2026-09-04: still true. It stops being a sleep once the deep-link handler exposes a settled signal the spec can wait for before reading the error list.

Three occurrences, and only two are waits. The 900ms between mouse.down and mouse.up IS the long press: a hold shorter than the threshold is a different gesture, so no seam can remove it and it should not be read as debt. The other two are the 2s entrance-stagger + liveQuery settle before the hold (a row remount mid-hold unmounts the LongPress span and clears its timer) and the 1s spacing between retries. Reviewed 2026-09-04: the settle needs a list-ready signal.

The 2s is the entrance stagger plus the post-seed liveQuery refresh settling, because a row remount mid-gesture resets SwipeRow's reveal state; the 1s is retry spacing. The gesture's own completion is already awaited deterministically through data-open. Reviewed 2026-09-04: the settle needs the same list-ready signal as long-press and should be paid down with it.

Flushes deferred translation calls before reading the collected missing-key errors. The assertion is about the ABSENCE of console output, which has no event. Reviewed 2026-09-04: still true; it needs the copilot panel to report hydration-settled.
